$comment: During the Events phase each player, in turn order, reveals one card and resolves it (see deck below). The card's scope decides who it hits: a global card the third player draws still hits everyone. Each card carries plain text for the tabletop game and a machine-readable effects array so the digital version can resolve it automatically.

scopes.name: Global
scopes.summary: Applies to every player, whoever drew it.

scopes.name: Local
scopes.summary: Applies to one region of the board - roll for the region.

scopes.name: Targeted
scopes.summary: Applies to the player who drew it - except crime cards, which target the leader.

scopes.name: Offer
scopes.summary: An opportunity. The drawer decides first; if they pass, it goes round in turn order.

effectTypes.$comment: The vocabulary the digital engine understands. Keep new cards inside it where you can.
effectTypes.effort: Change effort dice or hours for matching workers.
effectTypes.price: Shift a commodity family's price band.
effectTypes.building: Damage, destroy or halt a building.
effectTypes.tool: Add wear to or break tools.
effectTypes.health: Damage or heal characters and travelling figures.
effectTypes.discovery: Widen or shrink a result band on the discovery tables - see data/discovery.json.

cards.name: Hard Frost
cards.text: A cold snap grips the map. Crops stall and outdoor work is miserable.

effects.text: Every growing crop stalls: nothing advances for one round.
Every worker on tundra, mountain or hills produces 1 less effort.

mitigations: Workers living in a brick house or manor are unaffected.
A town with 2+ fuel in stock ignores the effort penalty.

cards.name: Drought
cards.text: The wells run low. Nothing green does well this year.

effects.text: Every crop in the region yields half when it is harvested.
Every town in the region loses 2 water.

mitigations: A town with a well loses no water.
Towns on a marsh tile, or waterside on a river or a lake - anywhere with fresh water - are unaffected.

cards.name: Long Summer
cards.text: A gift of a season.

effects.text: Every growing crop advances one step, free.
Every worker produces 1 more effort.

cards.name: Storms at Sea
cards.text: Nothing sails this round, and something already at sea does not arrive.

effects.text: No ship or barge moves for one round.
Every ship at sea loses half the cargo tokens aboard it.

mitigations: Cargo in a harbour tile is safe.

cards.name: Flood
cards.text: The river takes back its floodplain.

effects.text: Every crop growing on a farm in the region is destroyed.
Every building on a river hex in the region stops for one round.
Silt: a small consolation.

cards.name: Earthquake
cards.text: The hills shrug.

effects.text: Halve the build track - the building stops until it is repaired.
Nothing crosses a mountain hex for two rounds.

cards.name: Wildfire
cards.text: Fire runs through the timber.

effects.text: Roll a d6 for every timber building in the region: on 4 or more it burns down.
Every town in the region loses 4 logs.

mitigations: A town with a well or on a water-access tile rolls at 5+ instead.

cards.name: Mine Collapse
cards.text: A gallery comes down.

effects.text: One of your mines stops for two rounds while the gallery is dug out.
One worker is lost.

mitigations: A dwarf player halts for 1 round and loses no worker.

cards.name: Warehouse Heist
cards.text: Thieves empty a warehouse in the night.

effects.text: Lose half the contents of one warehouse, owner's choice of which items.

mitigations: A watchtower in that town cancels this card once per game.
Soldiers garrisoned in the town halve the loss.

cards.name: Caravan Robbery
cards.text: Bandits on the road.

effects.text: The highest-value cargo token in transit by road is taken.

mitigations: An escorting soldier rolls a combat die; on 4+ the robbery fails.

cards.name: Train Heist
cards.text: They knew the timetable.

effects.text: Three quarters of the cargo tokens on that train are taken, highest value first.
That line carries nothing for one round.

cards.name: Piracy
cards.text: A sail on the horizon, and it is not a friendly one.

effects.text: Every player loses half the cargo tokens they have afloat, highest value first.

cards.name: Smuggling Ring
cards.text: Someone offers to move goods without the market's cut - and without any guarantees.

effects.text: Sell up to 6 bulk at 150% of base value.
Gain 1 unrest.

cards.name: Wolf Pack
cards.text: Something is taking the livestock.

effects.text: Every pasture in the region loses 2 sheep.
A wolf pack, strength 2, is placed in the region and stays until it is killed.

mitigations: Any soldier or hero in the region may fight the pack instead of losing animals.

cards.name: Boar in the Fields
cards.text: It has been in the crops for a week.

effects.text: One crop on one farm in the region is destroyed.
Gain 3 meat.
Spend 3 effort.

cards.name: Dragon Sighting
cards.text: A shape passes over the mountains. Everyone finds somewhere else to be.

effects.text: Nothing crosses a mountain hex for two rounds.
A dragon, strength 8, settles on a random mountain hex and stays there.
Panic buying of portable wealth.

cards.name: Raiders
cards.text: An armed band comes over the border at whoever looks richest.

effects.text: Raiders, strength 3, attack one of the leader's towns.
If the defence fails, that town loses a quarter of everything in it.

mitigations: Palisade grants +1 defence die. Garrisoned soldiers defend automatically.

cards.name: Border Dispute
cards.text: Two towns claim the same ground.

effects.text: Lose a tenth of the stock in one of your towns.
Both players roll 2 combat dice. The loser gives the winner one tile's worth of infrastructure.

cards.name: Mercenaries for Hire
cards.text: Swords, cheap, for as long as the coin lasts.

effects.text: Two soldiers join you for three rounds, then they leave.

cards.name: Plague
cards.text: It moves faster than anyone can plan for.

effects.text: Every town in the region loses a quarter of its workers.
Workers in the region roll one die step lower for two rounds.

mitigations: A town holding a Healing Draught spends it to ignore this card entirely.

cards.name: Migrants
cards.text: A column of families on the road, looking for somewhere with food.

effects.condition: you must have housing and 4 food in that town
effects.text: Two workers join a town of yours that has housing and 4 food to spare.
Gain 1 unrest.

cards.name: Strike
cards.text: They want feeding properly.

effects.text: Any town of yours with 1 or more unrest produces half its effort for one round.

mitigations: Serve ale or wine at an inn to end the strike immediately.

cards.name: Festival
cards.text: A week of noise and spending.

effects.text: Drink goes up two bands.
Luxuries go up one band.

effects.condition: if the town serves any drink
effects.text: Every town that can serve a drink loses 1 unrest.

cards.name: Travelling Master
cards.text: A master will take an apprentice, for a price.

effects.text: Train one specialist without a guildhall.

cards.name: Iron Shortage
cards.text: Everyone wants metal and nobody has any.

effects.text: Metal goes up two bands for three rounds.

cards.name: Glut
cards.text: A bumper year somewhere else. Prices fall through the floor.

effects.text: Food falls two bands for two rounds.

cards.name: Foreign Demand
cards.text: A distant city sends buyers. Roll to see what they want.

effects.text: Roll for a commodity family: it goes up two bands for two rounds.

cards.name: Tax Levy
cards.text: The crown remembers you exist.

effects.text: Pay 3 coin per completed building. If you cannot pay, gain 1 unrest per unpaid building.

cards.name: Ley Surge
cards.text: The ground hums for a week.

effects.text: Every town with an alchemist gains 1 mana crystal.
Every worker rolls one die step higher for one round.

cards.name: Curdled Brew
cards.text: Something went wrong in the alembic.

effects.text: One of your towns loses every arcane herb in it.
One alembic of yours is broken and comes off the board.

cards.name: Wandering Wizard
cards.text: He will trade knowledge for something shiny.

effects.text: Take any 2 potions from items.json for free.

cards.name: Camp Fever
cards.text: Something in the water at last night's camp. Your travelling party wakes shivering.

effects.text: Every figure and character in one of your travelling parties takes 2 damage.
That party moves half as far for one round.

mitigations: A healer character in the party shrugs it off: no damage, full speed.
Spend a Healing Draught or Physic Tonic to cancel the card.

cards.name: Marsh Ague
cards.text: The ague drifts out of the fens with the evening mist, and the village bell rings thin all week.

effects.text: Workers in the region roll one die step lower for two rounds.

effects.condition: only towns on or adjacent to a marsh tile
effects.text: Every town on or beside a marsh loses one worker.

mitigations: A town with an infirmary and a fed healer loses no worker.
A Physic Tonic cancels the card for one town.

cards.name: The Grey Pox
cards.text: It starts in one market square and is everywhere by week's end. Whole streets shutter; the carts stop coming.

effects.condition: every town with 4 or more workers loses one
effects.text: Every town with 4 or more workers loses one.
Every worker rolls one die step lower for one round.

mitigations: A town with an infirmary and a fed healer loses no worker.
A Healing Draught spent by a town cancels its loss.
This is the card that makes the infirmary worth its parchment.

cards.name: Impure Smelt
cards.text: A bad seam of flux stone in every furnace this week. The metal pours grey and snaps like slate.

effects.text: Every tool used this round takes double wear.
Any tool forged this round is marked brittle: it breaks when its durability track reaches half, not zero.

mitigations: A smelter or blacksmith burning coal this round is unaffected - coal runs hot enough to burn the impurities out. Peat and charcoal do not.
A smith specialist may spend 2 hours re-tempering to clear one brittle mark.

cards.name: Blood Moon
cards.text: The moon rises rust-red and the wild things move under it.

effects.text: Monster bands on every discovery table widen by 3 for two rounds.

mitigations: A party carrying a lit lantern is never surprised: it may always choose to withdraw before a monster encounter begins.

cards.name: The Quiet Season
cards.text: The wild goes still. Hunters come home early, and nothing follows them home.

effects.text: Monster bands on every discovery table shrink by 2 for two rounds.

cards.name: Black Sails on the Horizon
cards.text: A squadron under no flag anyone will name works the sea lanes for a season.

effects.text: Every player with cargo at sea loses one cargo token - highest value first.
Anything that has to come by sea gets dearer.

mitigations: A ship with a Warded Hold or an escort of 2+ soldiers keeps its cargo.
A player whose shore hex is patrolled by a befriended Reef Serpent is not touched.
Cargo sitting in a harbour is safe - it just is not moving.

cards.name: Letter of Marque
cards.text: A seat of government will licence one privateer, and look away.

effects.text: Take it: for the next 3 rounds your ships may take one cargo token per round from any other player's ship in an adjacent water hex, and keep it. Every other player gains 1 unrest in every coastal town of yours they can reach, and your ships pay double harbour fees for the rest of the game.

mitigations: Passing costs nothing. The card goes round in turn order and is discarded if nobody takes it.
A victim may buy the letter back from the holder at any agreed price; the licence is a piece of paper, and paper is tradeable.

cards.name: Press Gang
cards.text: They came for the harbour taverns at midnight and left with whoever could walk.

effects.text: Two workers are gone. They may come back - see the mitigation.
That town gains 1 unrest.

mitigations: A town with a palisade or a garrison of 1+ soldiers loses nobody.
A town with an inn loses one worker instead of two: the innkeeper hides the regulars in the cellar.
Roll d6 at the end of each following round; on a 6 the pressed workers walk home.

cards.name: The Dragon's Tithe
cards.text: Vhalrik has counted, and finds the Reach behind on its payments.

effects.text: Every player hands over 1 gold, 1 gems or 2 jewellery, their choice, from any one town. A player with none of those loses their highest-value commodity stack instead.
Any player who refuses places Vhalrik on their richest town. He attacks it at the start of the next round.

mitigations: A player who has befriended Vhalrik pays nothing and may not be attacked by him.
Paying is always allowed and always ends it. That is the lesson.

cards.name: The Aerial Post
cards.text: A postal contract, offered to whoever can actually fly it.

effects.text: Take it if you own an airship: 40 coin now, and 15 coin at the end of every round in which that airship ends its leg at a different settlement from the one it started at. Miss two rounds running and the contract is cancelled.

mitigations: Only a player with an airship may take it. If nobody has one it is discarded, and shuffled back in ten rounds later.
Cancelling costs nothing but the contract.

cards.name: Gale
cards.text: It comes off the ice and does not stop until it reaches the sea.

effects.text: Nothing flies. An airship in the air when this is drawn marks 2 damage and comes down on the nearest land hex.
Ships and barges move half as far for one round.
Roll a d6 for every timber building on the board: on a 6 it takes 1 damage.

mitigations: An airship moored at a settlement takes no damage.
A ship in harbour is unaffected.
A sweep-rigged airship marks 1 damage instead of 2 - the crew can at least steer the descent.

cards.name: Early Thaw
cards.text: The frost lets go three weeks before anybody planned for.

effects.text: The winter rule in travel.json lifts. Any sled standing on marsh or water is lost with its cargo.
Every growing crop advances one step, free.
The fens are impassable to everything.

mitigations: A sled on solid ground is fine - it just becomes a box on runners until the next frost.
A player who moved every sled to a settlement last round loses nothing.

cards.name: Clipped Coin
cards.text: Somebody has been shaving the edges, and everybody knows it but nobody will be first to refuse a coin.

effects.text: Every price band shifts up one step. Prices are higher; the coin in your hand is not.
Every town with a market gains 1 unrest.

mitigations: A player holding gold, gems or jewellery instead of coin loses nothing to this - metal does not care what the mint says.
A trading house sets its own scales: its owner ignores the band shift for one sale.

cards.name: Guild Embargo
cards.text: You have undercut them once too often.

effects.text: Pick the commodity family you sell most of: you sell it at two bands worse for 3 rounds. Everyone else sells it at one band better.

mitigations: A player with a merchant or a trading house may pay the guild off: 60 coin, and the card is discarded.
Selling to another player instead of to the board sidesteps the embargo entirely - which is the whole point of having friends.

cards.name: New Tolls
cards.text: A gate, a rope and a man with a ledger, on a road you paid to build.

effects.text: 5 coin per cargo token entering or leaving the region by road, for 3 rounds. Pay, or go round.

mitigations: The player who built the road in that region collects the toll instead of paying it.
Rail, water and air pay nothing - which is how everyone learns what a road is worth.

cards.name: The Sign of the Green Man
cards.text: A failing inn on a good road, and an innkeeper who wants out.

effects.text: Buy it for 70 coin: place an inn, free of build cost and build time, on any road or route tile you have travelled, inside or outside a town. It is yours, it earns like any inn, and other players may use it at your price.

mitigations: Passing costs nothing.
A player who already owns three inns may not take it - see buildings.json inn, and the reason there is a cap.

cards.name: The Mead Run
cards.text: Every inn in the Reach is dry at once, and they are all offering above the odds.

effects.text: Sell any quantity of mead or ale this round at double the current band, to the board, from any town connected to a route - no market building needed.
Afterwards the cellars are full and the price falls a band.

mitigations: Passing costs nothing.
A player with an apiary and a brewery can usually take this twice a game, which is exactly the industry this card exists to make worth building.

cards.name: Ley Drought
cards.text: The ground has gone quiet. Nobody can say why, and the ones who can will not.

effects.text: Every town loses 1 mana crystal.
Every spell costs 1 extra mana for 2 rounds, and mana veins yield nothing.

mitigations: Mana already stored in a talisman is untouched - which is what talismans are for.
An elf holds their innate mana as normal.
A shrine in a town cancels the extra spell cost for characters standing in it.

cards.name: Boom Town
cards.text: A strike is announced, the road fills with hopefuls, and a village of forty becomes a town of four hundred in a month.

effects.text: The largest town in the region gains 2 workers.
Food and drink in that region jump two bands. Everyone has to eat and nobody planted anything.
Every town in the region gains 1 unrest.

mitigations: A town with a granary holding 4+ food ignores the price jump and gains the workers anyway - which is the whole argument for granaries.
The player who owns the nearest farm may sell into that region at the boom price. Demand is only a disaster if you have nothing to sell.

cards.name: The Frame-Breakers
cards.text: They broke the frames of the master who cut the rate, not his neighbour's. The letter was signed General Ludd.

effects.text: Every town holding 1+ unrest loses its best tool: broken, not worn. A town with none is walked past.
Pay 10 coin per unrest in that town. The unrest clears and the tool is spared.
20 coin to quarter them, the tool goes anyway, and the town gains 1 more unrest.

mitigations: A town holding no unrest is not visited at all. That is the whole card: the frames of a master who paid the rate were left standing in the same workshop as the ones that were broken.
An inn serving ale, or a granary holding 4+ food, clears 1 unrest in that town before the card resolves - a grievance settled at a table is not a grievance.
A player may make an example of the ringleaders: 40 coin and 1 unrest in every town they own, and this card is taken out of the deck for the rest of the game. It works, and it is meant to sit badly.
cards.history:
The Luddites were not against machines. Between 1811 and 1816 the framework-knitters of Nottinghamshire, the croppers of the West Riding and the weavers of Lancashire broke a great deal of machinery, and what they broke belonged to the masters who had cut the piece rate or put out shoddy work made by unapprenticed hands. Frames belonging to masters who paid the going rate were left standing, sometimes in the same room. The aim was the wage, not the engine.

They had asked first. The framework-knitters petitioned Parliament for their old rates and their apprenticeship customs, which had had statutory backing since 1563, and were refused; the apprenticeship clauses were repealed outright in 1814. Combinations of workmen were illegal under the Acts of 1799 and 1800, so a trade that could not lawfully bargain broke its employers' capital instead. Eric Hobsbawm called it collective bargaining by riot.

The answer was the Frame Breaking Act of 1812, which made breaking a stocking frame a hanging offence. Byron spoke against it in his maiden speech in the Lords on 27 February 1812 and asked whether there was not blood enough upon the penal code; the bill passed. Some twelve thousand troops went into the disturbed districts, more than Wellington had taken to the Peninsula four years earlier. At York in January 1813 seventeen men were hanged and others transported, and it stopped.

The name is a folk one: Ned Ludd, an apprentice supposed to have smashed two frames at Anstey around 1779, who probably never existed. The letters came signed General Ludd and dated from Sherwood Forest, which is a joke with a point on it. The modern sense of the word - somebody against new technology on principle - is very nearly the reverse of what the men who wore the name said they wanted, and that reversal is why this card is aimed by unrest and not by how mechanised anybody is.

deck.$totalNote: Sum of every card's copies, and it is generated rather than remembered: the figure has drifted twice already, which is exactly why the annex is built from this file.
deck.when: In the Events phase, each player in turn order reveals one card and resolves it before the Labour Roll.

lateGame.extra: From round 13, the first player each round reveals and resolves a second card.

deck.reshuffle: When the deck runs out, shuffle the discard pile and carry on.
designNotes: Every player turning a card means every player owns a piece of the round's weather. A global card is global whoever drew it; a targeted card is the drawer's problem.
Weather and market cards are the common ones - they should feel like the seasons turning, not like being punished.
Crime cards target the leader by default. That is the catch-up mechanism, and it is deliberate.
Every disaster card should have at least one mitigation a player could have bought in advance. Being wiped out should always be traceable to a decision.
Discovery-band cards (Blood Moon, The Quiet Season) are the dial on how dangerous the wild feels. Add copies to taste.
